title: Design: the Sales Type filter on Sales By Representative looks as designed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Scenario: Today has a split work order, a work order with one person on both sides and a part sale, and you compare the Sales Type filter with the design.
  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Today has one invoiced split work order (Labor {Sales-rep-A}, Parts {Sales-rep-B}), one invoiced work order with {Sales-rep-A} on both sides and one invoiced part sale with no shop supplies.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "sbr-06-a4-filter-open.png" (board 4.6) and "sbr-07-a4-sbr-labor-only.png" (board 4.7) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open for today in that browser window, with the Sales Type column turned on (as in the picture of board 4.7).
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open the Sales Type filter and compare with the picture of board 4.6.
  2. Select only Labor and compare with the picture of board 4.7.
  3. Select all three again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the filter lists "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales", all ticked.
  • Step 2: only the labor side of each work order shows, as in the picture.
  • Step 3: all three are ticked again and the filter reads "Sales Type: All".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative), story SV-11272 (Story 8, Filter both sales reports by Sales Type)

  • S8-R1: “Sales By Representative has a "Sales Type" filter with three options, in this order: "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales". All three are selected by default.”
  • S8-R3: “With all three selected the filter reads "Sales Type: All". With none it reads "Sales Type: None". Otherwise it reads the selected names in option order, for example "Sales Type: Labor, Parts".”
  • S5-R12: “With the Sales Type filter narrowed to Labor or to Parts, only that side's row shows (Story 8).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

  • Design — board 4.6 title: “4.6 The Sales Type filter”
  • Design — board 4.6 note: “Labor, Parts and Part Sales, all on by default. Rows and every total follow it; any combination works.”
  • Design — board 4.7 title: “4.7 Labor only”
  • Design — board 4.7 note: “"Sales Type: Labor" keeps only the labor side of each work order. (The Sales Type column is switched on in this board, from board 4.9.)”
